protocol: Four CPU worlds, seed 101, continuous default 16 commands, 6 seconds each, 1 second warmup. Same original play randomization/noise and legacy COM composition. Each pair changes only the added local class-driver position bounds.
scope: Small paired dynamics screen, not a held-out promotion suite or installed-hardware validation.

limitations: Installed Pi driver, robot description and calibration remain unknown. These bounds are an explicitly named local class-source contract.
Four randomized worlds at one seed do not establish broad robustness or statistical significance.
Original foot/knee-only collision model and legacy COM composition remain unchanged; no torso clearance or independent COM robustness is claimed.
The earlier GPU candidates were trained with controller limits only. Extra driver limits here alter dynamics without retraining.
interpretation: The local class-driver clamp changes behavior materially without causing falls in this small screen. Both checkpoint pairs have zero failures and identical realized randomized parameters; this does not establish a general failure bound.
Mixed baseline mean segment XY error increases from 0.10452 to 0.12258 m/s. At the -1.5 m/s command, achieved reverse velocity drops from -0.855 to -0.606 m/s; most low-speed segments change little.

Fast candidate mean segment XY error remains nearly unchanged, 0.06334 to 0.06366 m/s, but positive-turn yaw error increases from 0.182 to 0.229 rad/s and positive-lateral XY error increases from 0.092 to 0.128 m/s. Aggregate averages obscure these directional regressions.

Fast remains a candidate, not a promoted policy: the larger controller-only GPU suite already rejected it for reverse-speed failure and torque/slip/low-speed regressions. This small new screen cannot overturn that finding.

Recommendation: preserve the in-progress bootstrap stage at its completion boundary, then redirect remaining training to an explicitly named driver-limit contract. Keep completed legacy comparisons immutable and evaluate corrected candidates against matched corrected-contract baselines before promotion.

Post-hoc signed torso-to-plane distance is positive in all 64,000 scored states across the four screens; minimum clearances are recorded per run. This supports retaining the existing simplified collision model for this flat-plane screen only. It does not establish Bumpy clearance or real robot body dimensions.
